title: U.S. House · New York's 7th Congressional District
area: Parts of Brooklyn and Queens, including Bushwick, Williamsburg, Greenpoint, Ridgewood, Sunnyside, Long Island City, and Bedford-Stuyvesant.

context.text: There is no incumbent in this race; Rep. Nydia Velázquez did not seek re-election. Claire Valdez defeated Antonio Reynoso, Julie Won, and Vichal Kumar in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 56.2% to 35.6% to 6.3% to 1.7%.

Antonio Reynoso had automatically advanced from the Working Families Party primary based on write-in votes before the Democratic primary was decided. After losing the Democratic primary, Reynoso withdrew from the Working Families Party line; Ballotpedia lists him as a withdrawn/disqualified candidate for the general election. Claire Valdez appears on the November 3 general-election ballot on both the Democratic and Working Families Party lines.

Melvin Rivera automatically advanced from both the Republican and Conservative Party primaries, which were canceled. He was also initially certified on the No Kings Party and Arts & Culture Party lines, but Ballotpedia lists those two lines as withdrawn/disqualified for the general election; Rivera appears on the ballot on the Republican and Conservative lines.

candidates.name: Claire Valdez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 56.2% of the vote
candidates.currentRole: Member, New York State Assembly, District 37 (since 2025)

summary.text: Claire Valdez is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee in the open NY-7 race. A Texas native who moved to New York City in 2015, she worked at Columbia University, became a union unit chair with UAW Local 2110, and was elected to the New York State Assembly (District 37) in 2024. She describes herself as a democratic socialist and is running on labor organizing, universal rent control, Medicare for All, and abolishing ICE.

background.text: Originally from Lubbock, Texas (born 1989, per Wikipedia); moved to New York City in 2015 to pursue a career as a visual artist, according to a New York Daily News profile. Holds a BFA from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, per Wikipedia.
Took an administrative job at Columbia University, where she became active in her union, United Auto Workers Local 2110.

Worked as a union organizer and served on the bargaining committee of UAW Local 2110 at Columbia University; elected Unit Chair in 2022 to represent about 500 coworkers, and took part in the effort to elect reform candidates to UAW leadership, according to her Assembly biography.
Joined the New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America in 2019, per Wikipedia; her campaign website describes her as a "proud democratic socialist."

Won the June 2024 Democratic primary for New York State Assembly District 37 over Johanna Carmona and incumbent Juan Ardila, and the November 2024 general election; took office January 1, 2025. The district includes Long Island City, Sunnyside, Woodside, Maspeth, and Ridgewood.
Assembly committee assignments for 2025-2026: Alcoholism and Drug Abuse; Cities; Social Services; Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development; Transportation.

Announced her campaign for Congress in January 2026 after Rep. Nydia Velázquez announced her retirement, and won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Antonio Reynoso, Julie Won, and Vichal Kumar.
Endorsed in her 2026 congressional campaign by U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the Justice Democrats, and NYC-DSA.
Lives in Ridgewood, Queens, according to her Assembly biography.

priorities.text: "Building a thriving labor movement is really gonna be the key to defending our democracy," and says she wants a federal government that supports union organizing, citing her own experience as a former UAW Local 2110 member.
In Congress, Valdez will fight to strengthen and pass the PRO Act, establish federal support for union organizing, and end "at will" employment.
She will sponsor Medicare for All on "Day One" in Congress.
She will fight to dismantle and abolish ICE and push for immigration reform that legalizes the status of millions of immigrant Americans.

positions.summary: Campaigns for universal rent control and greater tenant power, and as an Assemblymember is the prime sponsor of a bill to cap initial regulated rents at the average for comparable rent-stabilized units.
positions.quote: In Congress, Claire will fight for: Universal rent control

positions.summary: Supports a full supply of homes through public investment, as part of a housing platform centered on universal rent control and tenant power.
positions.quote: A full supply of homes through public investment

positions.summary: Will sponsor Medicare for All in Congress, aiming to guarantee health care regardless of employment.
positions.quote: Claire will sponsor Medicare for All on Day One and fight the insurance companies that profit from denying care and driving up costs.

positions.summary: Opposes expanded immigration enforcement; campaigns to abolish and dismantle ICE and push for immigration reform that legalizes the status of millions of immigrant Americans.
positions.quote: Claire Valdez will fight to dismantle and abolish ICE.

positions.summary: Opposes continued U.S. military aid to Israel and calls for an end to weapons sales tied to the conflict.
positions.quote: Push to end all weapons sales and military aid to Israel and fight for Palestinian freedom.

positions.summary: Calls for guaranteeing a job with a living wage as part of a broader labor and economic security agenda.
positions.quote: Ensure everyone has the freedom to live a good life by guaranteeing a job with a living wage, paid parental and sick leave, quality health care, and a dignified retirement.

positions.summary: Supports a Green New Deal-style transition, including freezing electricity rates and rapidly investing in clean, publicly accountable energy.
positions.quote: Call for freezing electricity rates, holding corporations accountable, and investing in a rapid transition to an affordable, clean, and reliable energy system

record.text: Prime sponsor of A08084, which would place limitations on initial regulated rents so they do not exceed the average rent for a comparable rent-regulated housing accommodation; referred to the Assembly Housing Committee (as of January 2026, not yet passed).
Prime sponsor of A05427, which would protect tenants displaced due to fire; referred to the Assembly Housing Committee.

Prime sponsor of A08917, which would prohibit employers from using workplace surveillance tools to monitor employees in private, off-duty areas or in a worker's residence or vehicle; referred to the Assembly Labor Committee.
Prime sponsor of A08931, which would require just cause for employment termination and restrict use of electronic monitoring for disciplinary purposes; referred to the Assembly Labor Committee.

Prime sponsor of A11160, which would repeal the property-tax exemption for private universities that receive real-property tax exemptions of $100 million or more; referred to the Assembly Real Property Taxation Committee.
Serves on the Assembly Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Cities, Social Services, Tourism/Parks/Arts/Sports Development, and Transportation committees for the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.name: Melvin Rivera

summary.text: Melvin Rivera is a Brooklyn-born community organizer and tenant advocate running for the open NY-7 seat as the Republican and Conservative Party candidate. According to his campaign website, he has been a community activist for more than 30 years and served in the Mayor's Public Engagement Unit in 2020. He is running on tenant-to-homeownership conversion (TOPA), an anti-flip tax, public safety funding, and an apprenticeship-based approach to public assistance, and describes himself as running independent of party loyalty.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was born at Greenpoint Hospital and was raised in Bushwick, Brooklyn, in the 1980s.

Began community work with his first job as a high school student at the YMCA and, per his campaign website, has been a community activist for more than 30 years, working with at-risk youth, seniors, and people with special needs.
Says he helped create tenant associations and cease-and-desist zones in East New York and Cypress Hills, and is helping develop legislation for an Anti-Flip Tax.
Says he assisted families displaced by Hurricane Maria in 2018 with housing, benefits, and employment connections.

Says that in 2019 a management company (Riseboro) mismanaged his rent-stabilized building and neighboring properties into foreclosure, and that he organized tenants across nine buildings targeted by New York City's Third-Party Transfer program, protecting the affordability of more than 150 rent-stabilized apartments.
Served in the NYC Mayor's Public Engagement Unit during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 as a Social Distance Ambassador.
Helped organize community opposition to National Grid's proposed North Brooklyn Pipeline in 2020.

His campaign biography says he experienced homelessness earlier in life and chose to run as an independent; Ballotpedia lists him on the November ballot as the Republican and Conservative Party candidate (also on the No Kings Party and Arts & Culture Party lines), after the Republican primary was canceled.

priorities.text: "Shift from renter instability to ownership, stability, and community control."
Proposes a Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act (TOPA) giving tenants first right to purchase their building, plus an anti-flip tax and expanded cease-and-desist zones against real-estate speculators.
Calls for fully funding law enforcement with increased officer salaries and mental-health support alongside community engagement.
"[a] competitive economy that works for workers, not monopolies."

positions.summary: Supports tenant-protection measures including cease-and-desist zones against real-estate speculators and an anti-flip tax, framed as protecting existing tenants from displacement.
positions.quote: Shift from renter instability to ownership, stability, and community control.

positions.summary: Supports a 'balanced' enforcement approach targeting people with criminal records and requiring warrants, while also proposing expedited Green Card pathways for long-term, law-abiding, tax-paying residents.
positions.quote: A system that is lawful, humane, and practical.

positions.summary: Proposes fully funding police departments with higher officer salaries and added mental-health support.
Supports tenant-to-owner conversion policy (TOPA) as a path to expand homeownership and community-controlled housing rather than new market-rate construction specifically.

record.text: Says his community organizing helped draft legislative proposals for an Anti-Flip Tax intended to deter housing speculators from quickly reselling properties in working-class neighborhoods; the bill has not been introduced in Congress as Rivera does not currently hold office.

candidates.researchNotes: Rivera has not held elected office, so there is no floor-vote or bill-sponsorship record to cite; entries above reflect his own account of community organizing work, which could not be independently verified beyond his campaign site.

candidates.name: Priscilla Ghaznavi

summary.text: Priscilla Ghaznavi is an independent candidate running on the Our Future Party line in NY-7. According to her campaign website, she is a designer who has worked for seven publicly traded companies and is a former president of her homeowners association. She campaigns on housing affordability and homeownership, expanded mental-health care, and property-tax relief tied to income rather than market value.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C., to immigrant parents from Iran and Bolivia; has lived in New York City for more than three decades, in Chelsea, Greenpoint, and Williamsburg, according to her campaign website.

Holds a bachelor's degree in Marketing with a concentration in International Trade, plus additional qualifications in design, merchandising, and advanced studies in Milan, according to her campaign website; was elected President of New York State DECA during college. Ballotpedia lists associate and bachelor's degrees from the Fashion Institute of Technology.
Describes a career as a designer spanning seven publicly traded companies in business and creative leadership roles.
Served as president of her homeowners association, where her campaign says she stabilized its finances during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Earned a fourth degree, in Entrepreneurship, in May 2026, according to her campaign website; fluent in English and Spanish ("Castellano"), per the same page.

priorities.text: "Housing is the foundation of stability, and homeownership is the pathway to generational wealth."
"Healthcare should be a fundamental human right, and access should be made available for every person."
Campaign centers on three pillars: opportunity, accountability, and access.

positions.summary: Supports expanding access to affordable housing and homeownership for working families.
positions.quote: I will advance policies that expand access to affordable housing and homeownership for working families while ensuring property taxes reflect income realities rather than just rising market values.

positions.summary: Supports treating health care access as a fundamental right, with an emphasis on expanding community-based mental-health services.
positions.quote: Healthcare should be a fundamental human right, and access should be made available for every person.

candidates.researchNotes: Ghaznavi has not held elected office (aside from a homeowners association presidency) and has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; her campaign website does not state clear positions on immigration, guns, abortion, climate, or foreign policy, so those issue keys are omitted rather than inferred.
